title: Splenic regulation of systemic platelet activation state.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: No data files exist to open. I checked Europe PMC (open-access flags all N: not in PubMed Central, hasSuppl=N, hasData=N, no text-mined accessions), NCBI elink from PubMed ID 42752134 (only paper-to-paper links, no GEO, SRA, BioProject or BioSample), GEO by keyword and by author, BioProject, PRIDE (proteomics archive, 0 hits), Zenodo, Dryad and figshare searches on the title and DOI (all empty), and HEAD requests on the three standard Science supplementary-file URL patterns, which all returned HTTP 403 (access forbidden).
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Everything about the science: that the spleen filters activated platelets in mice, that glycoprotein VI (a platelet collagen receptor) drives activation in the splenic red pulp, and that G6b-B inhibitory signalling triggered by perlecan lets quiescent platelets recirculate. All of this comes from the 178-word abstract; I could not read the methods, figures, supplementary tables or any data availability statement.

a1_downloadable.note: No downloadable data of any kind. The paper is paywalled and not in PubMed Central; Europe PMC reports no supplementary files and no linked data; GEO, SRA, BioProject, PRIDE, Zenodo, Dryad and figshare searches on the title, DOI and senior authors returned nothing; the publisher's supplementary URLs return HTTP 403. A1 fails outright.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Not assessable, and almost certainly fails anyway: the implied label (platelet retained in spleen versus recirculating) exists only inside flow-cytometry gates and intravital microscopy movies, none of which are deposited, so it would have to be constructed from raw instrument output.

a3_inputs_present.note: Not assessable. No feature file exists; inputs would be flow-cytometry marker intensities or image-derived measurements that are not public.

a4_units_stated.note: Not assessable. No files, no column headers, no units seen.

a5_enough_rows.note: Unknown and unverifiable. A mouse intravital-imaging and flow-cytometry study of this kind typically yields tens of animals per condition; the modelling unit would be the mouse or the imaging field, far below the ~1,500-row bar, though single platelet events could in principle number more.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Not assessable. If the intravital microscopy movies were ever released they would likely be tens to hundreds of gigabytes, but nothing is available to size.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Not assessable. Nothing to count against the paper, and the paper's own numbers are behind a paywall.

a8_label_provenance.note: Not assessable. The label would come from microscope and cytometer readouts via the authors' own gating and segmentation choices, which are not documented in anything I can read.

honest_claim_h3: No claim is possible: there is no accessible data behind this paper.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use a platelet's surface activation markers to predict whether the spleen will trap it or let it return to the blood.
plain_idea.train_on: The project I considered would train on individual mouse platelets, each described by its activation-marker readings (for example P-selectin and active integrin levels measured by flow cytometry, a laser-based single-cell counting method) plus the mouse's condition. Number of examples: unknown, because no data file is public.
plain_idea.predict: A yes/no outcome: captured and retained in the spleen versus recirculating. The true answer would come from the authors' intravital microscopy (live imaging of the spleen in an anaesthetised mouse) and from counting labelled platelets before and after splenic passage.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Haematologists and cardiovascular groups would like a rule for which platelets the body itself removes, because it predicts who carries a high load of hyperreactive platelets and therefore thrombotic risk. In practice none of this is testable here, since the measurements were never deposited.

ml_idea: Considered and abandoned: classify single platelets as splenically retained versus recirculating from their activation-marker profile, and regress the whole-animal fraction of activated platelets on splenic filtering capacity. Both need the raw flow-cytometry and imaging data, which does not exist publicly.

effort.compute_note: No estimates possible; no files were obtainable to size or time.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Query Europe PMC for open-access status and linked data, then NCBI elink from the PubMed ID. Both came back empty in under a minute, which kills the project.

verdict_reason: Part A1 fails: the paper is paywalled, absent from PubMed Central, and has no deposited data in GEO, SRA, BioProject, PRIDE, Zenodo, Dryad or figshare; the publisher's supplementary files return HTTP 403. Even if the supplement were open, this is a mouse imaging and flow-cytometry study whose modelling unit would be a handful of animals per condition, so A5 would very likely fail too.
